verdicts.conditionQuote: It assumes you already run the service behind a load balancer.
verdicts.claimQuote: This tutorial walks through a blue-green release of `orders-api`
verdicts.note: A prerequisite scoping the whole tutorial; no single claim becomes false without it.

verdicts.conditionQuote: The cost is running twice the infrastructure during a release
verdicts.claimQuote: You keep two identical production environments, called blue and green.
verdicts.note: A cost of the approach; the description stays true.

verdicts.conditionQuote: returns `200` only when the service can reach its database and its queue
verdicts.claimQuote: Poll the health endpoint on every green instance until all of them return `200`.
verdicts.note: A prerequisite on what the health check means; the health gate relies on it, but the step itself stays true.

verdicts.conditionQuote: Database migrations that are backward compatible, so the old version keeps working against the new schema. This is a hard requirement: both versions share one database, and a rollback does not undo a migration.
verdicts.claimQuote: Because the old environment is still running, going back is the same one-step switch.
verdicts.note: With a non-backward-compatible migration, switching back to blue does not restore a working service.

verdicts.conditionQuote: If any migration is not backward compatible, do not use this procedure
verdicts.claimQuote: you deploy the new version to the idle one, test it there, and then move traffic over in one step
verdicts.note: Excludes the whole procedure in that case; overlaps c4.

verdicts.conditionQuote: using the same build artifact that passed staging rather than a fresh build
verdicts.note: A constraint on how to perform the step; could also be read as procedural detail (not_a_condition).

verdicts.conditionQuote: once, from a single job rather than from every green instance at startup
verdicts.claimQuote: Apply the database migrations from the new release
verdicts.note: A constraint on running migrations; the step stays true but must carry it.

verdicts.conditionQuote: If any instance is still failing health checks after 10 minutes, stop here and roll back: tear down green and leave blue serving traffic.
verdicts.claimQuote: Poll the health endpoint on every green instance until all of them return `200`.
verdicts.note: Without the 10-minute stop-and-roll-back rule the step implies waiting indefinitely and then proceeding to the switch.

verdicts.conditionQuote: If one fails, treat it like a failed health check and stop.
verdicts.claimQuote: Send the smoke-test suite to green's internal address. Expected result: all smoke tests pass.
verdicts.note: Gate on proceeding to the traffic switch.

verdicts.conditionQuote: If the error rate rises above 2% at any point in that window, switch back
verdicts.claimQuote: Observe the 5xx error rate on green for 15 minutes after the switch.
verdicts.note: The threshold and window define when to roll back; 'continue' is true only if the rate stays at or below 2%.

verdicts.conditionQuote: Leave blue running, unchanged, for 24 hours. It is your rollback target until then.
verdicts.claimQuote: Because the old environment is still running, going back is the same one-step switch.
verdicts.note: One-step switch-back holds only while blue is still running, i.e. for the 24-hour standby.

verdicts.claimQuote: A rollback before step 5 is cheap, because customers never saw green.
verdicts.note: Intra-sentence scope; the cheapness claim is false after step 5. Could also be read as just a statement, not a limit.

verdicts.conditionQuote: requests that were in flight on green during the switch may fail and need a client retry
verdicts.claimQuote: A switch-back after step 5 is also fast
verdicts.note: A cost of a late switch-back; it is still fast.

verdicts.conditionQuote: Do not run the next release's migrations while blue is still on standby. If you do, the standby may no longer work against the schema, and the switch-back stops being a safe option.
verdicts.claimQuote: It is your rollback target until then.
verdicts.note: Blue is not a safe rollback target if the next release's migrations run during standby.
